entries.21112e4dfea3a0d8: This recipe posting and search service addresses the question "What should I cook today?" It has a feature called "Tsukurepo" for recommending dishes that users have made, and introduces popular keywords; it can be used for free. As paid features, it offers popularity-ranked search, which shows popular recipes, and suggestions of recipes by daily menu and theme, among others. The securities report states that monthly usage fees paid by paid members of the recipe service account for most of revenue, and that for the fiscal year ended December 2025, the continued decline in premium service members was the main cause of the revenue decline.
entries.225788a77016f525: Users are people who search for or post cooking recipes (free users and paid members), people who receive cooking advice through moment, and people who buy ingredients through Cookpad Mart. The filing states that there is no external customer whose revenue from transactions with a single external customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue. The filing also states, in its business risks section, that collection of fees for paid services is entrusted to mobile carriers and mobile app distribution platform providers, among others.

entries.5dfa3b3d31471c4f: “Cookpad” is a recipe posting and search service. It can be used free of charge and offers paid features such as popularity-ranked search that shows popular recipes, and suggestions of daily menus and recommended recipes by theme. “moment” is a service in which an AI camera analyzes the cooking steps in the user's home kitchen, identifies problems and their causes, and returns advice tailored to the user. “Cookpad Mart” is a system that delivers ingredients to dedicated refrigerated delivery boxes installed in apartment buildings and other locations, allowing users to collect them along their daily routes.

entries.69d42ee6c4f62ee5: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥5,336 million, down 9.2% year on year. The previous year was ¥5,876 million. The notes to the filing state that the majority of revenue is recipe service membership revenue, consisting of monthly usage fees paid by paid members, and that revenue is recognized over the period in which services such as popularity-ranked search are provided. Management's analysis attributes the main cause of the revenue decline to continued decreases in premium service members. The filing does not state the revenue of moment or Cookpad Mart.

entries.6db3954536c25bfb: This service aims to resolve the shopping challenge of "difficulty obtaining fresh, high-quality ingredients." It has set up a system in which products are delivered to dedicated refrigerated delivery boxes installed in apartment buildings and other locations, so that users can pick up ingredients along their daily routes. The securities report states that while the significance and potential were confirmed to a certain extent through building relationships with producers and evaluating quality, a model that simultaneously achieves reproducibility, scalability and profitability has not yet been established, and that for the fiscal year ended December 2025 it has not become a clear growth driver.

entries.71df63c41a9c16a4: Cookpad Inc. operates mainly the recipe posting and search service “Cookpad,” together with “moment,” an AI camera-based cooking coaching service, and “Cookpad Mart,” a home delivery service for ingredients. The filing groups the business into one [[term:segment|segment]], “Business to Make Everyday Cooking Enjoyable,” and does not show revenue for each of its three services. The majority of revenue comes from monthly usage fees paid by paid members of the recipe service. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥5,336 million, down 9.2% year on year, and operating profit was ¥264 million.

entries.885225ab125d5173: This is an AI camera-based cooking coaching service that aims to eliminate the gap between knowledge and practice, namely the feeling of "being unable to cook well." An AI camera analyzes the cooking process in the user's home kitchen, identifies where the issues are and why they arise, and returns specific advice tailored to the user. The securities report states that for the fiscal year ended December 2025, while it gained positive results from experiences tailored to individual growth, progress was delayed at the stage of offering it as a general-purpose product.

entries.aff277f49354dd45: The company has its head office in Meguro-ku, Tokyo, and has set “Making Everyday Cooking Enjoyable” as its mission. The filing states that the articles of incorporation provide that the company exists for this mission and that “The company will dissolve when everyday cooking has become enjoyable in every household in the world.” The company and its [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] comprise six companies in total, and consolidated employees as of December 31, 2025 were 101 (temporary employees, with an annual average of 17, are not included in this figure).

entries.b620382d342ae32e: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥264 million (¥673 million in the previous year, down 60.8% year on year). Selling, general and administrative expenses were ¥5,022 million (down 2.6% year on year), and the filing explains that personnel costs fell with the natural decline in the number of employees and that cost reductions from company-wide efficiency measures progressed. As a breakdown, the notes to the consolidated financial statements list employee benefit expenses and remuneration, system usage fees, outsourcing costs and sales commissions. Although operating profit declined, financial income from securities investment increased, so profit before income taxes was ¥1,098 million (down 1.0% year on year), at a level similar to the previous year (the breakdown of financial income is gains on securities and interest income). Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥741 million (down 44.4% year on year), and the filing states that this was affected by, among other things, the reversal of deferred tax assets resulting from a cautious review of estimates of future taxable income. The filing also states that the current structure is one in which the recipe service membership business generates profit, and cites strengthening other profit bases as an issue.
